method: goldenRows(trunkImpl): trunk's own resolvers, cut from that tree's sidecar/index.js and run over its providers/registry.js and engine-credential.js (test/helpers/credential-store-sandbox.js)
legend: One row per station. A label names what each layer holds: K = the desktop shell's push (the keychain layer), E = the operator's environment, P = the browser page's copy; k = a key, u = an endpoint, p = backup keys (a key pool).

A run is label=key@endpoint[backup keys], resolved as runOnceCore resolves the pair it is handed. st = the station's own choice as a gate reads it (runKey undefined); kc, en, en2, br, sk, pg = a run handed that layer's key; fo = a body key no layer holds; fo+u, pg+u = a body key sent with an endpoint in this request; pg+u.rec, kc+u.rec = a record handing that key back with an endpoint; +u = a keyless body naming an endpoint.

Keys: kc keychain, en / en2 bare env names, br STARNET_ spelling, sk SKYNET_ spelling, pg page, fo foreign, li linked; pools kc.p, en.p, pg.p (and kc.p1, en.p1, pg.p1). Endpoints: kc, en, br, sk, pg, ex = http://<code>.test/v1, li = the linked URL + /v1, def = the profile default, - = none.

pres = engine-key presence: keySource / saved key, backup count, endpoint / unattendedReady. held = the keys a channel record would have dropped as station-held (channelKeyIsStationHeld). foreign = channelEndpointIsForeign for the page key beside http://ex.test/v1, the page URL with a trailing slash, and no URL. alias = the runtimeKey mirror.

desktop rows: each push (provider/endpointPersisted), the kept endpoints, file reads, verified writes, log lines, the providers with no endpoint handed over yet, and the endpoint each resolves. push rows: what each push left in the keychain layer and how each provider resolves after it.

Trunk's pool crossings were pinned as they were until step S4: R1 = layers custom K:- E:p P:kup (st= and pg=: the env pool rode the page key at the page endpoint), R6 = layers custom K:up E:- P:- (fo=: the pushed pool rode a body key). Both are delta D2 rows now. A step changes rows only as named golden deltas (D1 S2, D2 S4, D3 and D4 S7).

shell rows (step S2): the desktop shell's spawn shapes under its marker (STARNET_DESKTOP_SHELL=1, the IPC token) beside a user's own exports, then a push. A label names the provider, what the environment holds (pair = both spellings with one value, what the shell writes; single = one spelling; split = two values; bare = the plain name; a pool pair = KEY_POOL_<ID> in both spellings) and the push. st, pres and alias as above; held = which of kc, kc2, os, br, sk, kc.p1, en.p1 count as station-held. kc = the keychain key, kc2 its rotation, os a bare export, br / sk one spelling's value.

The shell table holds THIS LANE's rows. Trunk ignores the marker: every row deltas.D1 does not list is what trunk gives for the same station (captured on a3af8dafd0be808b1abb52ec330d99152278c162), and the same stations without the marker resolve the same at the tip, both under the pool rule in force at step S2 (deltas.D2 then moves the pools of some, S4). deltas.D1 lists each row the marker changes, with trunk's value, the value now and why.

deltas.D2 (step S4): every row the pool binding moves. Its was map gives, for each run of the row whose backup keys moved, the pool that run had before S4 (trunk's, for the six trunk tables; S2's, for the shell table, whose rows D1 also lists where the marker changed them); the row in tables has the pool now. why: R1 = an env KEY_POOL that rode a key the environment does not hold, R6 = a keychain pool that rode a key the keychain does not hold, own = the run now rotates on its own layer's backups, which the other layer's pool displaced, sent = a key sent in this request takes only a pool sent with it (runOnceCore's key-pool line).

deltas.D3 (step S7): every row the complete-pair rule moves, with the whole row as it was before S7 (was; S4's pools are already in it, so where deltas.D2 lists the same row its old pools are read off this one). why: P3b = an env key with no endpoint hid a saved page pair, K = a keychain key with no endpoint hid one. Only CUSTOM stations trunk refused move, and on each only the station's own run, a keyless body and presence.

deltas.D4 (step S7): every refusal the rule changes. A row's station has the same key and no endpoint before and after, so D4 is about what index.js's engineCredentialError says for it ('this routine'), which no table column shows: trunk is the sentence from trunk's own function, now the sentence here. An env key with no endpoint was told no base URL is saved, which was false beside a URL the page saved with no key (probe P3c, decision 5), and whose exit led there.

D2.what: A key pool rides only its own layer's key: the keychain pool the keychain key, the env KEY_POOL the env key, the page copy's backups the page key. A key a caller sent gets only a pool sent with it, and a pool whose layer holds no key is unused (the keychain pool after the shell's REMOVE). At trunk the pushed pool and the env KEY_POOL rode any run key, so a refused key rotated onto another layer's account at that key's endpoint (probes R1 and R6). Only backup keys move: no row's key, endpoint, presence or held keys changes.

reasons.R1: an env KEY_POOL rode a key the environment does not hold: the page key at the page endpoint (probe R1), the keychain key, a body key, a channel's own key, or no key at all
reasons.R6: a keychain pool rode a key the keychain does not hold: a body key (probe R6), another layer's key, or no key at all (the shell keeps the pool's slot after a REMOVE; it is unused)
reasons.own: the run now rotates on its own layer's backups, which the other layer's pool displaced
reasons.sent: a key sent in this request (an /api/run body key) takes only a pool sent with it: here none, never the station's pool for that key

D3.what: The station's own choice is a complete pair: the first layer, in key order, whose key has a usable endpoint, used whole. A provider that needs a base URL looks past a key with no endpoint to the first lower layer with both, so key(id, '') and baseUrl(id, '') read one choice and a gate and the run it admits agree. Only stations trunk refused move: a key that has an endpoint keeps its place, and a page key never outranks a usable env key.

reasons.P3b: an env key with no endpoint hid the page's saved pair: every routine was refused 'no CUSTOM base URL is saved' with the URL saved (probe P3b, gh#137, gh#113)
reasons.K: a keychain key with no endpoint hid the page's saved pair (the keychain endpoint and the env URL are station-wide, so a keychain key with neither has none)
